covers: What happens steps 1-3
What should happen: told plainly why they cannot be signed in and what to do

items.reason: This is the ticket's exact reproduction: five wrong passwords lock the account, and the correct password was then answered with "Invalid username or password". It must run on e2e because the defect is the message the shopper reads on the Identity sign-in page, and Identity.API has no in-process test project. subject: BUG-55
reason: Council (testPlan, blockOn any, pass 9/10): not passed; opus 9/10, sol 7/10; 3 finding(s) stand, 4 note(s).

items.reason: Delete this case. TC-BUG-55-02 already submits a first wrong password and requires both the invalid-credentials message and absence of a lockout message; TC-BUG-55-01 also checks the invalid-credentials message.

Delete this case. TC-BUG-55-01 already checks the correct-password response during an active lockout and asserts the same message conditions. Seeding a distant lockout date adds no distinct contractual outcome, and this case does not advance time or repeat an attempt later to establish coverage across the lockout window.

The case explicitly requires preserving lockout and rejecting correct credentials. No ticket line requires this; 'What should happen' permits either successful sign-in or a plain explanation with an action. Remove the mandatory-refusal case and make retained scenarios accept either contractual outcome. Apply that correction to TC-BUG-55-01's mandatory refusal and TC-BUG-55-06's prerequisite that the locked account must be refused.

TC-02 step 2 already asserts 'Invalid username or password' after each wrong password and that no 'locked' text appears at any point; TC-07 (one wrong password -> Invalid, no 'locked') adds no new branch. Merge or drop it.

TC-01 already asserts that the correct password during lockout leaves the browser on /Account/Login with no signed-in header, which catches a fix that ignores lockout. TC-04 checks the same behaviour on a seeded lockout; fold its sign-in-state assertion into TC-03 instead of keeping a separate case.
The index and covers call TC-02 the 'boundary just inside the lockout limit', but it uses 2 wrong attempts while the limit is 5. Use 4 wrong attempts for a real boundary, or drop the boundary claim.

The ticket's complaint is 'no hint that waiting would help'. Asserting only 'locked' and 'try again' lets through a message such as 'Account locked, try again' that never says to wait. Also assert the message contains 'wait' (case-insensitive) in TC-01 and TC-03.
